Feature release for **uun**: it can now work **fully offline** from signed monthly snapshots of [endoflife.date](https://endoflife.date) data.

## New

- **Choose where EoL data comes from** with `eol_source` in `~/.config/uun/config.toml` (#18):

  | `eol_source` | Network use |
  |---|---|
  | `"api"` (default, as before) | Live per-product queries to endoflife.date |
  | `"bundle"` | One download of the newest signed monthly snapshot from this repo's `eol-YYYY-MM` releases |
  | `"offline"` | None. Import snapshots yourself with `uun --import-eol` |

- **Snapshot built into the packages.** These packages contain the latest verified snapshot. A fresh install has EoL data from the first run, even with no network.
- **`uun --import-eol FILE`** checks a snapshot's OpenSSH signature against the key shipped with uun, re-validates its contents, then uses it. Anything that fails leaves your current data untouched. (#18)
- **No silent downgrades.** uun refuses a snapshot older than the data it already has. Use `--allow-older` to go back on purpose. (#18)
- **Data age at a glance.** The title bar shows which data is in use, e.g. `EoL data: bundle 2026-11, 9d old`. It turns yellow and says "stale" once the data is older than `stale_days` (45). `--report` prints the same line, and `--report --json` gains an `eol_data` object. Exit codes are unchanged. (#18)
- **Monthly signed snapshots.** A GitHub Actions workflow publishes a snapshot on the 3rd of each month as release `eol-YYYY-MM`. Each one has a build-provenance attestation and can be checked by hand with `ssh-keygen` alone. See [docs/eol-data.md](https://github.com/nc-intezra/uun/blob/v0.2.0/docs/eol-data.md). (#13, #14, #16)

## Upgrading

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
sudo apt install ./uun_0.2.0-1_all.deb            # Ubuntu / Debian / Raspberry Pi OS
sudo dnf install ./uun-0.2.0-1.noarch.rpm         # Fedora / RHEL / Rocky / Alma
sudo zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm ./uun-0.2.0-1.noarch.rpm   # openSUSE Leap
```

Nothing changes unless you set `eol_source`; existing configs and caches keep working. For an offline machine:

```bash
install -d -m 700 ~/.config/uun                      # uun refuses group-writable config dirs
printf '[general]\neol_source = "offline"\n' >> ~/.config/uun/config.toml
uun --report | head -1                                # EoL data: bundle YYYY-MM, …
# later, with a newer snapshot copied over (both files):
uun --import-eol uun-eol-2026-12.json                 # reads uun-eol-2026-12.json.sig alongside
```

Signature checks need OpenSSH's `ssh-keygen`. The packages now recommend `openssh-client` / `openssh-clients`, which almost every system already has.

## Packages

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `uun_0.2.0-1_all.deb` | Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 12 / 13, Raspberry Pi OS bookworm+ (arm64 and armhf) |
| `uun-0.2.0-1.noarch.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL / Rocky / Alma 9 (installs `python3.11`+ automatically), openSUSE Leap 15.6 |
| `uun-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl`, `uun-0.2.0.tar.gz` | `pipx install` / pip on any Linux with Python ≥ 3.11 (no built-in snapshot; use `"api"` or `"bundle"`, or `--import-eol`) |
| `SHA256SUMS` | checksums for all of the above |

Each package was install-tested in clean environments for every distro listed, as an unprivileged user. The tests covered offline mode with the built-in snapshot, live end-of-life data, and clean removal. The packages still aren't GPG-signed, so check them against `SHA256SUMS`.

**Full changes:** https://github.com/nc-intezra/uun/compare/v0.1.1...v0.2.0
